title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 6 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Reading for Comprehension and Critical Reading
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: Practice passage: Should Schools Ban Cellphones? (original text; the survey and principal are fictional)
context.text:
In 2023, a survey of 2 000 South African teachers found that seven out of ten believed cellphones distract learners during lessons. Some schools have responded by banning phones completely, locking them away in pouches until the final bell.

Supporters of a ban argue that phones fuel cyberbullying and make it almost impossible to concentrate when a notification can interrupt every few minutes. One principal in Pretoria claims that marks at her school rose after the ban, although no independent study has confirmed this.

Yet a blanket ban seems an old-fashioned answer to a modern problem. Phones are powerful learning tools: dictionaries, calculators, cameras and libraries in a pocket. Surely the wiser choice is to teach young people to use them responsibly, rather than to pretend that the digital world stops at the school gate?

sections.title: QUESTION 3: Argumentative, Discursive and Reflective Essays
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: Example argumentative paragraph (original)
context.text: Firstly, a longer school day would leave learners exhausted rather than educated. Research on adolescent sleep shows that teenagers already struggle to get the eight to ten hours they need. Adding another hour of lessons would mean less time for homework, chores and rest, so learners would arrive at school even more tired. Therefore, extending the school day is likely to harm, not help, learners' results.

sections.title: QUESTION 4: Poetry Analysis
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: The Last Taxi Home (an original poem written for FreeSheet)
context.text:
The city exhales its final breath of day;
the robots blink their tired amber eyes.
At the rank, the vendors fold their stalls away,
and pigeons count the crumbs beneath grey skies.

My mother waits, her handbag on her knee,
her shoes still dusty from a stranger's floor.
She scrubbed their kitchens bright for them to see,
then caught the train, and now she waits once more.

The last taxi swings in, its music loud,
and she climbs in, a queen without a crown.
She does not know I watch her from the crowd,
or how I'll build her palace in this town.

questions.memo:
✓ The mother is compared to a queen (1)
✓ She has dignity, strength and worth (1)
✓ but no wealth, power or recognition (no crown) (1)
